name: joyce
desc: Emulates the Amstrad PCW on Unix, Windows and macOS
why: A full emulator of the Amstrad PCW word processor machine running on modern Unix, a time capsule you can actually boot.

brief.what_it_is: JOYCE is an emulator of the Amstrad PCW, the all-in-one word processor computer, for Unix, Windows and Mac OS X, written in SDL. It runs the PCW's CP/M environment and emulates its hardware, and it incorporates ANNE, an emulator of the later PcW16. The homepage mentions PCW disc images in DSK format, host folders mapped as emulated drives, and host joysticks, and output goes to an emulated PCW screen, with printer output that can be written to PDF or PNG files. The page covers the emulator and its downloads, plus a set of PCW hardware and software reference material.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit mission statement. It is the author's own project page (John Elliott's site, seasip.info) and is framed around keeping the PCW machine and its software usable, with a large reference archive of hardware, file formats and public-domain catalogues alongside the emulator.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals beyond saying it is written using SDL and that it incorporates ANNE for the PcW16. Its update history mentions a Z80 emulation, a MYZ80 hard drive emulation, and a GSX graphics driver, but it does not describe the architecture in detail.
brief.install_notes: The homepage lists Downloads and a FAQ, but the text I received did not include their URLs, so I did not follow them. From the page alone I found no install steps, runtimes or accounts. The brew executables are dskconv, dsklabel, lsgotek, xanne and xjoyce. The homepage mentions a configuration script in its history, and says the Windows build is a separate pack. Source builds on Linux and macOS are implied by the history notes about GCC, libpng and C++17 compile fixes.
brief.standout: It is a full hardware-level emulator of a 1990s word-processor appliance that also runs CP/M, and it has been kept current through a long run of releases. It also comes with an unusually deep archive of the machine's documentation and a security fix against malicious CP/M programs touching host files.
brief.status: Maintained. The most recent entry is v2.5.5 (development) dated 2026-03-26, with v2.5.4 in 2025-08-09 and v2.5.3 in 2024-03-26. The most recent stable release is v2.4.2 from 2023-05-21. The homepage was last updated 2023-03-25 by its footer, which the 2026 entry supersedes.
brief.caveats: The stable and development branches differ, and the newest features (PDF/PNG printing, PCW-Linkit, LocoLink) are in development releases. The homepage says the Gem Drive and Flash Drive hardware are not emulated, and its own emulated hard drive does not match any real hardware. The Windows and Unix builds are separate packages, and some releases were Linux-source-only with no new Windows pack. The homepage does not state a licence. The page says the software is not known to be ported to MacOS Classic or BeOS, only that SDL should make that possible.
quotes: JOYCE emulates the Amstrad PCW on Unix, Windows and Mac OS X.
Since it's written using SDL, it shouldn't be too hard to port it to other platforms such as MacOS Classic or BeOS.
If you use JOYCE / ANNE to run CP/M programs downloaded from the Internet, I recommend that you upgrade to this version.
fetch_log: https://www.seasip.info/Unix/Joyce/index.html - fetched OK; homepage text with update history and PCW reference index. Downloads, FAQ and other subpages were listed by name but their URLs were not in the returned text, so they were not followed.

judge.reason: A full emulator of an obscure word-processing computer that boots CP/M, paired with a deep archive of its hardware and software, makes computing history hands-on.

entry.title: Joyce
entry.tldr: An emulator of the Amstrad PCW, a 1980s all-in-one word processor that ran CP/M, kept alive with a deep archive of documentation.
entry.deeper_look:
JOYCE emulates the Amstrad PCW, a British word-processor appliance sold with a screen, keyboard, disc drive and printer in one box. It runs on Unix, Windows and Mac OS X and is written with SDL. It emulates the PCW's hardware, including a Z80 processor, so the machine's CP/M environment boots and runs the original software.

It works with PCW disc images in DSK format, and it can map host folders as emulated drives. Host joysticks are supported. Printer output can be written to PDF or PNG files, though the homepage places those features in the development releases. It also bundles ANNE, an emulator of the later PcW16, a different machine.

The project is John Elliott's, and the homepage gives no mission statement. It is framed around keeping the machine and its software usable, and the site carries a large reference archive of PCW hardware, file formats and public-domain software catalogues. The idea underneath is that an emulator doubles as documentation: to make old software run, someone had to write down exactly how the machine behaved.

One detail from the release notes: the author recommends upgrading if you run CP/M programs downloaded from the Internet, because a security fix stops malicious CP/M programs from touching host files.
entry.install:
brew install joyce
# installs the executables dskconv, dsklabel, lsgotek, xanne and xjoyce
# depends on libdsk, libpng and sdl12-compat; you need PCW disc images (DSK format) to have something to run

try_this.what_happens: Lists the command-line options for the PCW emulator.
Shows the options for ANNE, the bundled PcW16 emulator.
Shows how to convert between disc image formats.

entry.whats_unique: It emulates the hardware of a 1990s word-processor appliance that also ran CP/M, and it ships alongside an unusually deep archive of the machine's documentation.
entry.caveats: Stable (2.4.2) and development (2.5.x) branches differ, newer features like PDF/PNG printing are in development releases, and the Gem Drive and Flash Drive hardware is not emulated.
